title: ICAO Annex 6 (Aircraft Operations) and Annex 13 (Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation) Violations — Operational Irregularities in Flight LA8159 Boarding Denial
category: International Aviation / Human Rights / Treaty Law
allegation_summary: The operational handling of Flight LA8159 at Santiago Airport on July 5, 2024 presented irregularities that implicate ICAO Annex 6 (Operation of Aircraft) and Annex 13 (Aircraft Accident and Incident Investigation) standards. Annex 6 requires operators to establish procedures for passenger handling that ensure safety while respecting passenger rights. The removal of a passenger based on an unverified verbal allegation from a [[SPK-stewardess-accuser]] — without proper documentation, without review of available exculpatory evidence (CCTV), and without providing written reasons — contravenes the safety management principles in Annex 6. Additionally, the incident triggered security and safety procedures that warranted proper investigation under Annex 13 principles, yet no competent investigation was conducted by either DGAC or ANAC. The flight operations data (LA 0632, LA8159, and related flights) contained irregularities suggesting operational decisions inconsistent with ICAO standards.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for INT.ICAO.AN6.Ch3.3.1 and confirm excerpt
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: An operator shall establish procedures and instructions for the safe operation of aircraft, including passenger handling procedures that ensure safety while respecting the rights and dignity of passengers.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for INT.ICAO.AN13.Ch1 and confirm excerpt
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The sole objective of the investigation of an accident or incident shall be the prevention of accidents and incidents. It is not the purpose of this activity to apportion blame or liability.

verification_required: Fetch verbatim text for INT.ICAO.AN13.Ch5.5.1 and confirm excerpt
candidate_articles.preliminary_view: The State of Occurrence shall institute an investigation into the circumstances of the incident and shall be responsible for the conduct of the investigation.

candidate_articles.history_note: CRITICAL TEXTUAL ERROR: Chicago Convention Art. 26 deals with 'ACCIDENT' inquiries, not 'incidents.' The previous article_text paraphrased this as 'incident' — the canonical text uses 'accident.' Art. 26 also requires death, serious injury, or serious technical defect to trigger the obligation — a passenger-crew dispute does not meet this threshold. Downgraded from 'direct' to 'supporting.'
